author: reek
body: The spawn half of the kernel servicer: a child inherits its parent's FileSystem grant and reaches the disk only through the kernel servicer, because it holds no Device.Block of its own. This mirrors scope-runtime-spawn, but the write goes through the bare FileSystem effect op (the compiler-installed servicer) rather than fat16-* directly, so it pins that the servicer path -- not just the Device.Block path -- survives a fork: the write cap travelled with the child, and elevation reached the disk on its behalf.

author: reek
body: The parent is scoped to "OK" and does nothing itself. The child performs an in-scope write-file and reports the result: ten if it landed, zero if it did not. Ten is the only pass.

author: reek
body: An out-of-scope write is NOT attempted here: write-file is an effect op, so an out-of-scope path literal is a compile error (CDX4002), not a runtime refusal. The runtime scope path is pinned by scope-runtime-deny; this test pins cap inheritance and the servicer surviving a spawn.

author: reek
body: The effectful call sits in argument position rather than in a let: a let bound to a value with a concrete effect row is CDX2033, and poke-byte is itself effectful. Nest, do not bind.
